abstract: Epigenetic information is central to cellular identity, aging and rejuvenation. Unlike the relatively stable genomic sequence shared by most somatic cells, epigenetic states vary across cells and time, making their dynamics difficult to reconstruct from sparse experimental measurements. We introduce EpiState-T, the Temporal Epigenetic State Tensor, to represent selected epigenetic states across intervals and distinguish an observed trajectory from the use of a retained record. In a ten-cell simulation, an explicit reader can act on each cells surviving baseline record. Across 500 paired simulations, mean final distance to the cells own baseline was 0.736 with reading disabled, 0.182 with correctly assigned records and 0.402 with reassigned records. These differences follow from the specified reader. We separately applied the observation and transition tensors to 859,151 CpGs measured in three donor-associated fibroblast cultures before, during and after transient reprogramming. Among sites ending within 0.05 methylation units of baseline, 9.75-15.72% had first departed in treated cultures, compared with 5.37-9.91% in matched mock cultures. The intermediate measurement therefore distinguishes paths that an endpoint comparison merges. These are paths of population measurements: the human data do not track individual cells or establish that cells read a historical record. EpiState-T provides an initial mathematical framework for investigating temporal epigenetic information while keeping state representation, observed change and proposed biological mechanisms distinct.
